entries.title: II Samuel 5:1
segments: Then came all the tribes; David had before reigned over only the tribe of Judah.
Those who wait upon God in humble supplication and hearty obedience, will in due time, and in the best way, receive all which they need or can reasonably desire.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:2
segments: Feed my people; this is the first time a ruler is spoken of in the Bible under the emblem of a shepherd.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:3
segments: A clear definition and correct understanding of the mutual relations and duties of rulers and people tend to promote the stability of civil government and to increase its usefulness.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:6
segments:
Jerusalem; a portion of this city had continued to be inhabited by the Jebusites. 
 
  Except thou take--the blind and the lame; rather thus: Thou shalt not come in hither; but the blind and the lame shall take thee away; that is, though we had only the blind and lame, they could repel thee. 
 
Dependence on creatures is followed by sore disappointment; while dependence on God secures his blessing and leads to glorious success.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:8
segments: The lame and the blind; the Jebusites themselves, with allusion to their boast,

entries.title: II Samuel 5:9
segments: Millo; supposed to have been a apart of the fortress on mount Zion.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:11
segments: Tyre; a city of the Phenicians on the Mediterranean, near the northern border of Palestine.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:12
segments: Rulers are appointed and intrusted with authority for the good of the people, and are bound in all thier acts to seek this end.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:13
segments: Great prosperity increases the power of temptation, and often leads to great transgressions.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:17
segments:
The hold; a fortress, or fortified place. 
 
Such is the wickedness of men, that the increasing power and prosperity of one nation awakens the jealousy and provokes the hostility of another, and leads them to seek their own elevation by the depression or ruin of their neighbors.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:18
segments: Rephaim; a valley on the south-west of Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:20
segments:
Baal-perazim; meaning the plain of breaches; it was in the valley of Rephaim. 
 
One nation can gain no advantage over another, except such as God sees fit to grant, or for wise reasons to permit; and whenever he gives prosperity, he lays men under new obligations to obey him.

entries.title: II Samuel 5:25
segments: From Geba untl thou come to Gazer; in
we read, "from Gibeon even to Gazer."  Geba was a short distance north of Jerusalem, and Gibeon a short distance north-west.  Gazer was on the western border of Ephraim.
